newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac wanted Guillen on BoF council list - Monde.
newsitem.headline: Chirac wanted Guillen on BoF council list - Monde.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac wanted Pierre Guillen, former head of the CNPF employers' association, to be on the list of nominees for the Bank of France monetary policy council, afternoon daily Le Monde said on Wednesday.

Chirac and the French government are due to choose shortly from a list of six candidates put forward to fill two posts at the nine-member policy-making council. The presidents of the Senate, the National Assembly and the Economic and Social Council (CES) have submitted two names each.

Le Monde said Chirac had phoned Senate head Rene Monory on November 30 from Perigueux, southern France, where he was meeting German Chancellor Helmut Kohl "to express his surprise that Mr. Guillen was not on the list".

Sources familiar with the nomination process say that Guillen is one of two candidates proposed by CES head Jean Matteoli to the monetary policy council, along with Jean-Rene Bernard, formerly head of regional bank CIC and deputy governor of property bank Credit Foncier.

Monory said earlier on Wednesday that he wanted to reappoint ex-journalist and current monetary policy council member Jean Boissonnat along with Pierre Achard, economic counsellor at the French embassy in Bonn.

The sources said National Assembly head Philippe Seguin had put forward Robert Pelletier, formerly managing director of the Association of Credit Establishments (Afec) and Alain Prate, former vice-president of the European Investment Bank (EIB).
Seguin, whose own candidate, Paul Marchelli, became the most recent member of the monetary policy council, is seen as unlikely to get his nominees appointed this time round.
He had therefore persuaded Monory to put Guillen, who worked for Chirac during his election campaign, onto his own list, Le Monde said.
A spokeswoman for Chirac declined all comment on the Bank of France nomination process or the Le Monde report.
